platforms.deliverables: Basic tiers typically 2 sides (left/right) only; higher tiers add rear/front/roof, 3D mockup, source files (AI/EPS/PDF) and print-ready files. Example $25 basic: 2 sides, free mockup, all source files, unlimited revisions, 2-day delivery.
platforms.revisions: Varies by gig: commonly 3 or 'unlimited' in listings
platforms.turnaround: 1-3 days typical per listing (rush add-ons available)
platforms.ownership: Fiverr ToS default: buyer receives IP rights in delivered work upon payment unless the seller states otherwise on the Gig page; some gigs sell a separate 'For Commercial Use' license instead (perpetual, exclusive, non-transferable) or time-limited versions. Fiverr keeps right to use deliveries for its marketing. Check the gig page and order 'source file' + 'commercial use' extras.
how_to_find_good_designers: Search: 'van wrap design', 'vehicle wrap design print ready', 'Sprinter wrap', 'Ford Transit wrap', 'fleet wrap'
Filters: Seller level (Level 2 / Top Rated), Fiverr Pro, delivery time, budget; check gig reviews for photos of INSTALLED wraps
Confirm package includes all 4 sides + roof (if needed), vector source files, print-ready PDF at scale, and commercial use
Ask which template provider they use (Pro Vehicle Outlines / The Bad Wrap) for your exact van
cons: Quality highly variable; low tiers often 2 sides only
Some sellers lack wrap production knowledge (bleed, panel gaps, door handles)
Ownership/commercial rights can be gated behind extras

brief_checklist: Exact vehicle: year, make, model, trim (e.g. 2024 Ford Transit 250 / Mercedes Sprinter 2500), wheelbase (130in/148in/170in ext), roof height (low/medium/high), cargo door config (sliding side door left/right, barn vs lift rear doors, windows or panel)
Photos of all 4 sides plus measurements of the actual van; note dents, aftermarket racks, ladders, bulkheads, door handles, fuel cap, badges

Template: specify the template source (Pro Vehicle Outlines, The Bad Wrap, etc.) matched to the exact variant; buy and supply it if the designer doesn't have one; ask designer to verify against your measurements
Coverage: full wrap, partial (e.g. 3/4 or half), or spot graphics; which sides (driver, passenger, rear, front/hood, roof) - make sure the quote covers all of them
Brand assets: vector logo (AI/EPS/SVG/PDF), brand colours as Pantone + CMYK, fonts (licensed), photos at high resolution
Content hierarchy: business name, what you do (3-5 words), phone, website, QR code (test it), licence/registration numbers if required; readable at 50 ft and in 3 seconds

Deliverables: layered vector source files (AI/EPS) plus print-ready PDF per side, at 1:1 or stated scale (commonly 1:10 or 1:20 with scale noted), CMYK, fonts outlined, raster images embedded at sufficient resolution at final size (typically 100-150 dpi at 1:1), 3-6 in (75-150 mm) bleed beyond panel edges, no critical text across door gaps, handles or body lines
Mockups: realistic 3D or flat mockup of each side for approval
Production notes for any shop: panel layout/seam suggestions, colour profile, and a proof PDF; confirm with your chosen local shop which file format, scale and bleed they want before final export
Revisions and turnaround: number of revision rounds, deadline, rush fees

Ownership: written full copyright/IP assignment on payment, all source files delivered, commercial use with no restrictions, rights to reuse on other vehicles/fleet; confirm stock images and fonts are licensed for commercial vehicle use
Avoid design-tied-to-printing deals unless files are released (some shops, e.g. We Print Wraps, do not release print-ready artwork)
